title: The Churches in Revelation Were Warnings for Today
paragraphs: The Churches in Revelation Were Warnings for Today
You thought Revelation was only about the end of the world.
But before God revealed beasts, judgments, trumpets, and fire…
He spoke to the Church.
Not the world.
The Church.
Read that again.
Jesus walked among the lampstands and exposed what looked alive but was dying.
Ephesus had truth but lost love.
Smyrna suffered but stayed faithful.
Pergamum compromised.
Thyatira tolerated sin.

Sardis had a reputation for life, but Jesus said, “You are dead.”
Revelation 3:1
Philadelphia was weak, but faithful.
Laodicea was rich, comfortable, and spiritually disgusting.
Jesus said:

“Because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I will spit you out of my mouth.”
Revelation 3:16
God saw it.
You knew.

The private compromise.
The worship with no surrender.
The sermons without repentance.
The church attendance without obedience.
The Bible posts without brokenness.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Jesus didn’t warn them because He hated them.
He warned them because He loved them.

“Those whom I love, I reprove and discipline, so be zealous and repent.”
Revelation 3:19
That is the mercy of Christ.

He exposes before He removes.
He convicts before He judges.
He knocks before the door closes.

“Behold, I stand at the door and knock.”
Revelation 3:20
This is not a game.
A church can have lights, music, branding, programs, and crowds…
and still have Jesus outside the door.
The warning is not just for ancient churches.
It is for today.

For pastors.
For believers.
For the lukewarm.
For the religious.
For the ones who still know how to look saved while hiding sin.
Repent.

Not perform.
Not explain.
Not pretend.
Repent and return to Jesus Christ.
Because salvation is not found in church culture.
It is found in the crucified and risen King.

“In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses.”
Ephesians 1:7
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
Search your heart. Open Revelation 2–3. Let Christ examine what everyone else applauds.
